name: Build linked exits
summary: The unit places entrances that are linked to one another: a teammate who steps into one comes out of another, at once or after a short trip, so the team crosses the map without walking the ground between. Some versions are shelters where riders wait safely inside a network and choose their exit; others are pads that send one traveller at a time and then recharge. Every entrance can be destroyed, which closes it, and in harsh versions everyone still inside dies when the last one falls. In one variant the exit is the carrier that placed the shelter: recalling it brings everyone inside out beneath the carrier, wherever it is. Arrivals bunch up at a known exit that is easy to camp. Teleport moves the user or pulls teammates to them, placing no entrances; host-spawn-point brings back the dead.
counterplay: Find and break the ends: each entrance is a structure that ordinary fire destroys, and losing one closes that end of the link.

Camp the exit: travellers come out one after another at a known spot, so pre-aim it and put splash on it; Generals players strike the crowd at a tunnel mouth, and Natural Selection 2 marines fear a surrounded phase gate.
Kill the last entrance of a full network, or a garrisoned shelter: in the harsh versions everyone inside dies with it.
Watch for new exits: a worm breaking out of the ground is announced to every other player, and a fresh entrance is often weak while it forms.
Turn it against them: some links carry anyone (the Tiberium Wars wormhole, the Apex Legends rift), and Team Fortress 2 Spies ride enemy teleporters.

other_examples.unit: Tunnel Network (GLA) and the Sneak Attack power (Zero Hour)
other_examples.note: GLA workers can dig an entrance anywhere they can reach; all entrances open into one shared network, so ground units that go in at one can leave by any other, and entering restores their health. Each mouth has a small machine gun and comes with two rocket soldiers, but nobody can shoot from inside. When the last entrance falls everything inside is lost, and units leave by a single opening, so they bunch up for an area strike. Zero Hour's Sneak Attack power opens an extra entrance anywhere the player can see, open to attack while it breaks the surface, and a bought camouflage hides entrances from the enemy until they come under fire or a detector finds them.

The network grows worms that break out on any clear patch the player can see; every network and worm opens into one system, units inside can't be harmed and are lost only when every entrance is destroyed, and air units and allies can't use it. They leave singly, first in, first out. When a worm finishes surfacing, every other player hears a screech and gets a text warning; since Legacy of the Void a worm can't be hurt while it emerges.

The player picks two points, which stay joined for a short while; any ground unit, friend or foe, can go in at one end and come out at the other, and the power then needs a long recharge. A known trick is to open one beside an enemy construction yard and send a mind-controlling unit through to take it.

An Eldar building that infantry can step into; the player can later call those squads out of any of the side's gates, after a short delay. Researched upgrades let gates heal infantry around them and cloak nearby Eldar buildings, so a hidden gate can deliver troops where the enemy sees nothing.

sources.title: Dawn of War/Webway Gate, Dawn of War Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: The Engineer builds an entrance and an exit; a teammate who steps on the charged entrance appears at the exit at once, then the pair recharges, faster once upgraded. Travellers glow for a while afterwards, which betrays the exit; enemies can't use it except Spies, anyone standing on the exit when an enemy arrives dies, flag carriers can't travel, and a sapper put on one end also lands on the other. The Engineer scores a little each time a teammate uses it.

Marine phase gates work once two are built and powered: marines step in and arrive at the next gate in the order they were built, which the commander can reverse, and robots can't pass. Aliens attack gates first, and a gate placed against a wall can be surrounded so that arriving marines die on the spot. The aliens' tunnels join two entrances; marines can walk through as well but lose armour while inside.

sources.title: Phase Gate (Natural Selection 2), Natural Selection Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Symmetra sets an exit pad at a distance, linked to an entry pad at her feet; allies travel with the interact key while it lasts, enemies can shoot it down, it breaks if the two ends end up too far apart, and each traveller waits a moment before using it again.

Wraith drops one portal where she starts, runs a limited distance without being able to shoot, and drops the other; for a while anyone, enemies included, can travel through in either direction, safe from harm on the way but leaving a faint trail.

player_translation.summary: Press Q to plant an entrance, then a second one elsewhere: teammates who step into either come out of the other a moment later. Each end is a fragile structure the enemy can break, and the exit is a known spot they can camp. In the carrier variant you plant one shelter, and recalling it brings everyone inside out beneath you, wherever you are.
as_user: You build the team's shortcut: one end near where teammates respawn and one near the fight, so everyone gets back to the front in seconds.
Placement is everything: an exit behind cover keeps arrivals alive, while one in the open feeds them to a camper.
Network variant: teammates can wait inside safely and choose which mouth to come out of, so a stocked network can burst out on a flank.
Carrier variant: you set a shelter down where your team holds out, then fly off; when it is in danger, or when you have found a flank, you recall it and everyone inside appears beneath you.
You earn points for each teammate who travels, so building links pays even without kills.
as_target: Both ends are visible structures in the enemy's team colour: break one and the link closes.
Travellers come out one at a time with a flash and glow for a while afterwards: pre-aim the exit, and follow the glow back to it.
Network variant: destroy the last entrance and everyone inside is thrown out hurt, or dies in the harsh version.
Open-portal variant: you can use it too, to follow them back or to slip into their side.
teammates: Teammates choose to use it; a ping on the entrance shows where it leads.
Defenders guard both ends, and engineers repair them.
The other team sends a flanker or an infiltrator to break the far end, or to ride it into your base.
Paired with a forward spawn (host-spawn-point), a link lets a team hold a spot the enemy can't reach on foot.
controls: Q: plant the first end at your feet; Q again plants the second end within range; hold Q to pick an end back up and move it.
Teammates travel by walking onto an entrance or pressing E at it; in network variants a small menu picks the exit.
Carrier variant: Q sets the shelter down at the aimed spot; Q again recalls it after a short warning, setting everyone inside down beneath you.
feedback: Both ends glow in team colour, and the owner's team sees a line linking them on the minimap.
A flash and a sound at both ends whenever someone travels, and a glow on arrivals for a few seconds.
A health bar on each end and a warning to the builder when one is under fire.
Network and carrier variants show the owner's team how many are inside.
changes_from_rts: RTS networks hold whole armies, and in Generals, StarCraft II and the Thunderhead's Rod everyone inside dies when the last entrance or the shelter falls; with players inside, waits must be short and a lost link throws them out hurt, except in a harsh variant.
Generals workers can dig any number of entrances; two ends per builder, or a short chain, keep the map readable.
Exits need a moment of protection and a choice of direction, since a known exit is easy to camp, as Natural Selection 2's surrounded phase gates show.

The Thunderhead recalls its Rod from anywhere on the map, and the button is ready again after only a moment; the player version gives the shelter a short warning and the recall a delay, so it can't be a free escape from any fight.
Objective carriers can't travel, as Team Fortress 2 bars flag carriers from teleporters.

team_play.notes: A link is built for teammates: it carries respawned players back to the front, or a garrison onto a flank, in seconds. The builder's team must guard both ends, and the other team must hunt them.

notes: Two linked structures with their own health that share upgrades and, in some versions, sabotage.
Travel transitions: an instant hop for pads, or a stored 'inside' state for networks and shelters with a camera and an exit menu.
Exit placement checks and arrival rules against camping: a moment of protection and a spread of exit spots.
The carrier variant moves stored players to a moving carrier's position, with ground checks under it.
Rules for who may travel: enemies, objective carriers, vehicles.
Instant travel skips map design; ranges, recharge times and fragile ends are the levers.
A link into the enemy backline can put a whole team behind its defences; a visible far end and a build time keep it answerable.
Recalling a shelter from anywhere is a free escape; keep the warning and the delay.
Killing everyone inside when a network falls punishes several players for one builder's mistake.
Players must see that a structure is a linked end, and whose it is; the link line helps only the owner's team.
Arrivals must flash clearly, or teammates seem to appear from nowhere.
Several links on one screen confuse; a cap per builder keeps it readable.

variants.name: Pad pair
variants.summary: Two pads: step on the entrance and appear at the exit; the pair recharges between travellers, so it moves one teammate at a time.
variants.seen_in: Team Fortress 2 Teleporters; Overwatch Symmetra's Teleporter; Natural Selection 2 Phase Gates

variants.name: Tunnel network
variants.summary: Two or three mouths open into one shared network: teammates wait inside, safe and healing, and choose which mouth to leave by. If the last mouth falls they are thrown out hurt, or killed in the harsh version.
variants.seen_in: Generals Tunnel Network; StarCraft II Nydus Network; Dawn of War Webway Gate

adds_weaknesses.why: Everyone waiting inside is lost or thrown out together when the last mouth falls, and they leave by one opening where splash can catch them.

variants.name: Recall to the carrier
variants.summary: Set down one shelter that teammates garrison; on a key it dissolves and everyone inside reappears on the ground beneath you, wherever you are. If enemies destroy the shelter first, everyone inside dies with it.

adds_strengths.why: Pulls a whole garrison out of danger, or drops it onto a flank, at its own position in a moment.

adds_weaknesses.why: If enemies wreck the shelter before the recall, every teammate inside dies at once.

variants.name: Portal open to all
variants.summary: A short-lived pair of portals that anyone can use in both directions, enemies included: good for a raid, risky if the enemy follows.
variants.seen_in: Tiberium Wars Scrin Wormhole; Apex Legends Wraith's Dimensional Rift; Natural Selection 2 Alien Tunnels (marines lose armour inside)

variants.name: Burst-out exit
variants.summary: Open a new exit at a distant spot your team can see: it breaks out of the ground after a warning every enemy hears, then the teammates waiting inside pour out.
variants.seen_in: StarCraft II Nydus Worm; Generals Sneak Attack

variants.name: Run the link
variants.summary: Plant the first end, then run to the second spot, unable to fire, and plant the other; travellers follow the path you ran, quickly and safely.

variants.name: Hidden mouths
variants.summary: The entrances stay hidden from the enemy until a detector finds them or a fight breaks out at them, so a stocked network becomes an ambush.
variants.seen_in: Generals Tunnel Network with camouflage netting; Dawn of War Webway Gate's Shroud

countered_by.why: Detectors reveal the hidden entrances so they can be destroyed.
Once found, the single exit where arrivals bunch up is easy to blanket with splash.

adds_strengths.why: Gives teammates a fast, safe lane between two points it chooses, so reinforcements reach the front in seconds.

adds_weaknesses.why: Its ends are fragile structures the enemy can find and break, and arrivals come out at a known spot that can be camped.

counters.why: Moves teammates past minefields, hazard zones and held chokepoints instead of through them (reasoned: the link skips the ground between).

countered_by.why: Arrivals bunch up at the exit, so splash there catches several at once, as at Generals' crowded tunnel mouths.
Infiltrators ride enemy links into their base or sabotage both ends at once, as Team Fortress 2 Spies do with teleporters.

open_questions: Do teammates inside a network or shelter die when the last entrance falls, as in Generals, StarCraft II and the Thunderhead's Rod, or get thrown out hurt? (Recommended: thrown out hurt, with the harsh version only at high spice.)
May enemies use your links? (Recommended: no for pads and networks, yes only for the open portal variant.)
How long may a player wait inside a network or shelter before being pushed out?
Should the carrier variant's recall work from anywhere at once, as the Thunderhead's does, or need a delay and a warning at the shelter?

shooter_fit.reason: Team shooters already use teleporter pairs and portals well (Team Fortress 2, Natural Selection 2, Overwatch, Apex Legends), and two linked pads read clearly from above; exits need rules against camping, and networks need short waits.
